properties.value: the model in the caller's body is the model sent upstream
properties.tradeoff: no way to improve quality or cost automatically

properties.value: a target may forcibly rewrite any request field, including the model, and its value beats the caller's
properties.tradeoff: silent substitution: the caller is never told the model changed

properties.value: the fallback chain always starts at the first listed target and moves down one at a time
properties.tradeoff: the head of the list absorbs all load and all rate-limit pressure

properties.value: one target is picked at random in proportion to its weight, with a missing weight counting as 1
properties.tradeoff: load is balanced only in expectation; a saturated target keeps its full share

properties.property: no failover inside a balance group
properties.value: the target drawn at random is the only one tried; its error is returned as the group's answer
properties.tradeoff: resilience requires nesting the balanced group inside an explicit fallback chain

properties.value: a request can be steered by its metadata, body fields or URL path to a named target
properties.tradeoff: context lookup is exactly two levels deep, so deeper fields silently read as absent

properties.property: unknown target is a caller error
properties.value: naming a target that does not exist fails the whole request rather than falling through
properties.tradeoff: a config typo takes down live traffic instead of degrading

properties.value: there is no queue, so a request is either attempted immediately or answered with an error
properties.tradeoff: bursts are pushed straight onto the providers

properties.value: the gateway forms no opinion about saturation and forwards the provider's rejection
properties.tradeoff: no local shedding, so retry storms are possible

properties.value: quota is discovered only by being rejected
properties.tradeoff: every quota breach costs a full round trip

properties.value: a provider-supplied wait is obeyed only while the accumulated wait stays under one minute
properties.tradeoff: a long advertised wait is abandoned, converting a wait into a failure

properties.value: the provider's advertised wait is ignored entirely unless the config asks for it
properties.tradeoff: the default behaviour can amplify a rate-limit event

properties.value: a request is attempted once unless the config asks for more
properties.tradeoff: transient blips surface to the caller out of the box

properties.value: the config may ask for any number of attempts and the validator accepts it
properties.tradeoff: a single request can hold a connection and spend for a very long time

properties.value: all retries of all requests wait the same one, two, four second ladder
properties.tradeoff: synchronised retry waves after a shared outage

properties.value: only the listed status codes are retried; every other error fails instantly
properties.tradeoff: a misconfigured code list turns a recoverable error into a hard failure

properties.value: with no status list, a fallback group moves to the next target on any non-success, including a malformed or unauthorised request
properties.tradeoff: a bad request is replayed against every target in the chain

properties.value: an error the gateway itself raised marks the response so the fallback loop stops instead of retrying a doomed request
properties.tradeoff: an internal bug is never masked by a healthy second target

properties.value: each retry and each fallback hop is a complete new upstream call with no cancellation of the previous one
properties.tradeoff: one logical request can cost several completions

properties.value: a response that passed transport but failed an output check can trigger another upstream call from the same budget
properties.tradeoff: quality checks consume the availability budget

properties.value: a target that just failed is treated as fully healthy by the very next request
properties.tradeoff: during an outage every request pays the full failure latency before falling back

properties.value: the code leaves two hooks for an operator-supplied health layer and ships neither
properties.tradeoff: an open-source deployment has no quarantine at all

properties.value: the timeout restarts on every retry rather than bounding the whole request
properties.tradeoff: total latency is a multiple of the number the operator configured

properties.value: the timer stops once response headers arrive, so a stalled stream is never cut off
properties.tradeoff: streaming requests have no effective deadline

properties.property: timeout looks like an upstream answer
properties.value: exceeding the timeout produces a timeout response object rather than an exception
properties.tradeoff: that status is not in the default retry set, so a timeout ends the attempt chain unless configured

properties.value: two requests with wildly different deadlines are treated identically
properties.tradeoff: near-deadline work cannot buy priority

properties.value: each request brings its own routing config, so callers cannot see or affect each other's routing decisions
properties.tradeoff: it also means no shared view of the fleet and no fairness

properties.value: nothing reserves or caps any caller's slice of an upstream
properties.tradeoff: one noisy caller can consume a provider's whole quota

properties.value: cached answers are keyed by body and endpoint only, so they cross caller and provider boundaries
properties.tradeoff: a cache hit can serve one caller's completion to another

properties.value: nothing stops or slows a request because of what it will cost
properties.tradeoff: cost discipline must live outside the gateway

properties.value: an operator-supplied validator may veto a request before the upstream call and return its own response
properties.tradeoff: the veto runs after the guardrails and the cache, so those costs are already paid

properties.property: price is for the ledger only
properties.value: model pricing the host supplies is recorded in the log and never used to choose a target
properties.tradeoff: no cheapest-first placement is possible

properties.value: the decision depends only on this request's body, its headers and one random draw
properties.tradeoff: no adaptation, but trivially horizontally scalable

properties.value: a replay of a weighted-selection request can land on a different target
properties.tradeoff: incidents are not reproducible from the request alone

properties.value: memory grows with the length of the chain: one guardrail span and one log record per attempted target
properties.tradeoff: deep or heavily retried chains inflate the per-request footprint

properties.value: the optional response cache is a plain process-wide object that only evicts an entry when someone reads it after it expired
properties.tradeoff: unbounded growth, and it is the single piece of cross-request memory in the system

properties.value: the response names the exact config node that served it, so any nesting of strategies is explainable after the fact
properties.tradeoff: it says which node, never why that node: no weights, no draw, no scores

properties.value: abandoned retries are logged as first-class records rather than folded into the final one
properties.tradeoff: log volume multiplies with retries

properties.value: the reported attempt count becomes minus one when the budget ran out, instead of the real number of tries
properties.tradeoff: callers cannot distinguish one failed attempt from ten

properties.value: a bug in the gateway reaches the caller as a generic message with the cause only on standard error
properties.tradeoff: safe by default, hard to debug remotely

properties.value: a streamed response is recorded as a placeholder string, not content
properties.tradeoff: no post-hoc quality or cost audit of streamed traffic
